title: UC trace export (TypeScript): session and user must be copied to root-span session.id/user.id before export
answers: Why are my TypeScript traces exported to Unity Catalog missing from session search results?
How does the UC table exporter decide which session or user value goes onto the root span?
Where are session.id and user.id set for Unity Catalog traces in the TypeScript SDK?
Does the Databricks UC table span processor also export user_id or trace tags as span attributes?
body:
Path: Traces exported to a Unity Catalog OTel table go through libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/uc_table.ts:DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor (the onEnd path for the root span, which also handles updateTraceInfo and token/metadata aggregation before export).
Rule: DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor.setUserSessionSpanAttributes copies traceInfo.traceMetadata[TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_USER] and [TraceMetadataKey.TRACE_SESSION] onto the root span as SpanAttributeKey.USER_ID ('user.id') and SESSION_ID ('session.id') (libs/typescript/core/src/core/constants.ts:SpanAttributeKey). It runs before updateTraceInfo, and only when the metadata value is non-null. Add any new root-span attribute that UC search depends on in the same place.
Symptom: UC-backed TypeScript traces showed up in trace lists but were absent from session-filtered search, because UC session filtering reads the root-span attributes and the SDK only wrote the values into trace metadata.
Constraints: Applies only to the UC table exporter. The V3 MlflowSpanProcessor (libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/mlflow.ts:MlflowSpanProcessor) does not do this; its comment says V3 search reads user and session from TraceInfo metadata. Do not add the promotion there.
applies: TypeScript SDK, tracing export to Unity Catalog (UC table / OTLP otel spans); not the V3 MLflow tracking-server export path.
says: Client traces show up in catalog trace lists but vanish under session filters.
Filtering catalog traces by session returns no results for client-side recorded spans.
Catalog trace searches by user cannot find traces sent from the JavaScript client.
Make session and user filters in catalog trace search work for web client traces.
Exported catalog traces are missing from search results when filtering by user or session.
search: In libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/uc_table.ts:DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor.setUserSessionSpanAttributes, TRACE_USER and TRACE_SESSION from traceInfo.traceMetadata must be copied onto root spans as SpanAttributeKey.USER_ID ('user.id') and SESSION_ID ('session.id') when non-null prior to updateTraceInfo. This promotion enables Unity Catalog session-filtered trace searches to find root-span attributes. It applies solely to the TypeScript Unity Catalog table exporter, and must not be added to the V3 MlflowSpanProcessor in libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/mlflow.ts.
